- Restricts URL schemes to http/https only
- Blocks private, reserved, loopback, link-local, and multicast IPs

- create_webhook: reject SSRF targets before storing
- update_webhook: validate when URL is changed
- _deliver: re-validate at delivery time (anti-rebinding)

All three database backend variants (PostgreSQL, SQLite, MongoDB) are
covered by the same fix pattern.

* fix(upgrade): address review findings on the version-upgrade tooling

- reconcile: "we have no answer" is no longer read as "the target introduced
  this key". A recovered manifest carries only the ~14 keys recovery can infer
  from the file layout, so every other key looked new and was forced off —
  THEIRS rendered without the client's auth, database and i18n, and the merge
  deleted all of it. Unknown keys now fall back to the source version's
  defaults, which is exactly what BASE renders with.
- fetch/manifest: release tags are the bare version (0.2.16), not v0.2.16.
  The git fallback could never clone, and every manifest recorded a ref that
  404s.
- merge: run `git archive` with _SAFE_CONFIG. It honours the *global*
  attributes file even for the throwaway store, so a stray export-ignore
  silently dropped merged files (a new one made `git add` fail outright).
- cli: --force help now says it also overwrites colliding untracked files,
  and --path joins the misplaced-option guard (it has a default, so "was it
  typed?" needs click's ParameterSource).
- rename_guard: filter pairs with difflib's cheap upper bounds before the
  quadratic ratio(), so a release that reshuffles a directory can't turn the
  guard into a multi-minute CI job.

* fix(upgrade): deliver .env.example, survive gitignored merge output

- merge: `.env.example` is no longer treated as a secret. The `.env.` prefix rule
  swallowed it, so every new setting a release announces was dropped from the
  upgrade — silently, since classify_trees filters on the same predicate and no
  report line mentions it. backend/.env.example moved +24/-17 between 0.2.10 and
  now, all of it undeliverable.
- merge: stage with `git add --force`. Given an *explicit* pathspec covering an
  ignored path, `add` fails the whole call with exit 1, aborting materialize
  before anything lands. Reachable whenever a client ignores a path the template
  ships — including in the very upgrade that adds the ignore rule, since
  .gitignore is merged too. The pathspec list is exact, so forcing can only stage
  what the merge produced.
- merge: exclude .DS_Store / Thumbs.db. hatch force-includes template/ verbatim,
  so a wheel built on a Mac ships them and the upgrade adds them to every client
  repo.
- normalize: pin one Prettier config and ignore file across BASE/OURS/THEIRS, the
  frontend twin of the shared ruff config. Without it Prettier resolves each
  tree's own .prettierrc — the client's for OURS, the template's for the other
  two — so a tweaked printWidth makes every .ts/.tsx file read as a client edit
  and turns each real template change into a conflict.
- normalize: skip the same build/cache dirs the merge excludes.
  restore_generated_at walks the client's whole repo, so .ruff_cache/ and dist/
  were being read file by file.
- runner: validate --to. _parse_version degrades garbage to 0, so `--to nope`
  reported "Target vnope is older than v0.2.16. Downgrades are not supported.";
  canonicalizing also drops a typed `v` that would 404 on PyPI and the clone tag.

* fix(upgrade): correct the documented undo, warn on a dirty dry run

- docs: the "Undo at any point" command dropped the `-f` that undo_command()
  emits and explains. Following the docs with conflicts unresolved, `git checkout`
  refuses; once resolved it carries the *entire staged upgrade onto the user's own
  branch* and the next command then deletes the upgrade branch. Verified against
  git. Both sites (walkthrough + troubleshooting) also now clear the pending
  manifest, which the printed command already did.
- docs: `--force` also overwrites colliding untracked files — the CLI help says so,
  the flag table did not.
- runner: warn when `--dry-run` runs on a dirty tree. OURS is always the committed
  HEAD, so uncommitted edits are invisible to the preview; silently ignoring them
  lets a dry run promise zero conflicts that the real run (which requires a clean
  tree, so those edits get committed first) then produces. Prerequisites updated —
  they claimed a clean tree is always required, which is not true for --dry-run.

* fix(upgrade): a recorded rename must never overwrite the client's own file

apply_renames moves paths in BASE and OURS via shutil.move, which replaces its
target. So a client who independently created a file at the path the template
later renamed *into* lost it outright: the move overwrote their content, the merge
then saw one agreed path with no conflict, and nothing in the report mentioned it.

Occupied destinations are now skipped with a warning, degrading that one path to
the ordinary add/add the merge already surfaces. The directory branch no longer
rmtree's the source unconditionally either — that would delete whatever the move
loop skipped and turn the preserved file straight back into a silent loss.

* fix(upgrade): materialize the rglob scan before moving a renamed directory

rglob walks lazily via scandir, so moving files out from under it can drop
entries and leave part of a renamed directory behind — the exact edit loss
apply_renames exists to prevent.

* fix(upgrade): catch collisions with ignored files, prove .env.example delivery

- merge: the untracked-collision guard used `ls-files --others`, which honors

  `tar -x` overwrote it, and materialize()'s rollback never brought it back

  filesystem: anything in the merged tree that HEAD does not track but that exists
  on disk is a collision, ignored or not. Bounded by merged_files, so it never
  enumerates node_modules. Adding --force to `git add` last commit removed the
  accidental loud failure that used to follow this, so close the hole properly.
- merge: correct the skipped-rename docstring and warning. Measured: the
  destination becomes a modify/modify conflict and the un-moved original survives
  as a client-only file — not the "add/add" the comment claimed.
- tests: prove `.env.example` delivery through the whole merge → materialize path,

`_iter_text_files` matched the skip-list against `path.parts` of an *absolute*
path, so any ancestor named build/dist/venv/node_modules/... vetoed the entire
tree. A project at ~/build/myapp, a Docker WORKDIR /build or a CI checkout under
/builds/ got no normalization at all.

It failed asymmetrically, which is what made it a correctness bug rather than a
slowdown: the three rendered trees live under a tempdir and were still stripped,
but `restore_generated_at()` over the *client's* repo silently no-op'd — so
`<normalized-generated-at>` was written and staged into backend/pyproject.toml
and every alembic/versions/*.py header. Conflicted paths came out right (the
stage-blob rewrite is independent), clean ones came out wrong.

Match the skip-list against the tree-relative path, the way merge.is_excluded
already does, and make the two exclusion sets one constant so they cannot drift:
a dir the merge walks but normalize skips keeps its files unformatted in all
three trees, turning every template change there into a conflict.

Also: register the render shim dir for cleanup so each run stops leaving one in
/tmp, and stop pointing the untracked-collision error at `git stash` — the check
exists to catch ignored files, which stash skips even with -u.

* fix(upgrade): surface migrations the template rewrote, don't bury them

The guide promised "modified existing migrations are only flagged for review",
but nothing in the engine implemented it: `_MIGRATIONS_MARKER` was used solely to
route *brand-new* files into their own report section. A migration the template
changed landed in "Auto-updates" alongside thirty other paths and was applied
with no signal at all.

That is the one case where an automatic content update is dangerous. A migration
the client already has has almost certainly already run, and alembic keys off the
revision id — so the rewritten body never re-runs, and the file quietly stops
describing the schema it produced. The divergence surfaces later, as a migration
that "should have" applied a column that isn't there.

Keep applying the change (it lands on a branch, and a release does sometimes fix
a genuinely broken migration) but give it its own report section explaining why
it won't re-run and how to revert it. Conflicts still outrank the bucket — those
are already blocking and visible — and the client's own edit to a migration the
template didn't touch stays "Kept your changes".

Also correct the guide to describe what the code actually does, and point the
post-upgrade step at `make db-upgrade`, the target generated projects ship.

* fix(upgrade): normalization must reproduce what generation did

The post-gen hook runs `ruff check --fix` *and* `ruff format` when a project is
created; the upgrade's normalization ran only `format`. OURS therefore arrived
with unused imports stripped and `# ruff: noqa` headers removed, while the
freshly rendered BASE and THEIRS still carried them — so on a stock PostgreSQL
project 36 of 127 backend files differed with zero client edits in them. The
report labelled those "Kept your changes (template unchanged)", and the next
release touching any of their import blocks would have conflicted instead of
auto-updating: exactly the false-conflict flood this layer exists to prevent.

`normalize_tree` now takes `rendered=True` for BASE/THEIRS and runs the autofix
pass on those two only. Never on OURS — that would rewrite the client's own code
into the merged result, which is the reason the pass was skipped in the first
place. The check pass deliberately gets no `--config`: `--config <file>` moves
ruff's project root to that file's directory and re-orders imports differently
than generation did (measured: 7 residual mismatches with it, 1 without).

Measured on the same project: 36 spurious differences → 1, the real edit. The
report goes from 30 false "Kept your changes" to 8 honest "Auto-updates", and
the delivered branch content is byte-identical to before.

The self-upgrade e2e test could not see any of this because it built its
simulated client with `render_template` — the same unfaithful path the upgrade
uses for BASE/THEIRS, so the asymmetry cancelled. It now runs the hook's ruff
pair over the client, and fails without the fix.

Also fixed, both found while verifying the above:

- Generation and upgrade died under a non-UTF-8 locale. The empty-file sweep,
  `is_stub_file` and the `__init__.py` check all read rendered files with the
  platform default encoding, and the template ships 209 `.md`/`.mdx`/`.ts`/`.tsx`
  plus 163 `.py` files with non-ASCII content. On Windows cp125x or an
  `LC_ALL=C` container that is a `UnicodeDecodeError` through the whole
  generation, and through rendering BASE/THEIRS during an upgrade. All three now
  go through one `read_text` helper that reads UTF-8.

- `upgrade --path X finalize` told the user to put the flag before the
  subcommand, which is the form that had just been rejected. `finalize` and
  `recover` carry their own `--path`, so the message points there now; flags
  with no subcommand equivalent still say to drop it.

* fix(upgrade): a path must mean the same thing on both sides of the merge

The upgrade never checked that the project directory was its own git repository
root. Everywhere else the two halves of the merge disagree about what a path is:
`checkout-index` builds OURS from index paths (repo-root-relative) while
`ls-tree` through `git -C <subdir>` emits cwd-relative ones. For a project at
`monorepo/myapp` the rendered BASE/THEIRS shared no path with OURS, so every
template file read as a client deletion, the merged tree dropped it, and
materialize unlinked the client's real files and staged the deletions — no error,
and a report claiming the template had removed them. Refuse up front, dry runs
included, since the preview is wrong the same way.

The rename guard could also fabricate a rename and then pass itself: CI honoured
the `removed:`/`waived:` waivers in UPGRADES.yaml but record_renames.py only read
its own --waive, so a waived delete+add was written back as a rename and CI went
green because the move was now "covered". Both halves share recorded_waivers().
The stale-version check missed directory renames entirely — it matched exact
(from, to) keys, so a file covered by `a/ -> b/` was neither uncovered nor stale;
if that entry sat at or below the baseline the half-open range dropped it and a
whole subtree degraded to delete+add. It now resolves the covering entry.

Formatting symmetry across BASE/OURS/THEIRS is what makes the merge sound, and
both formatters already reported whether they ran — normalize_tree threw the
answer away. format_frontend bails when a tree already holds
frontend/node_modules (true for OURS if the client committed theirs, never for
the rendered trees), so Prettier ran on two trees of three and every .tsx read as
a client edit. normalize_tree returns FormattersRun and the run warns on
disagreement.

Also: files the client deleted no longer land in "Other changes (review on the
branch)" — a genuine no-op that read as "the upgrade lost my file" — and the
classification matrix is now exhaustive, with `other` kept only as a catch-all
and pinned by a test. finalize reports a corrupt or incomplete .pending instead
of raising KeyError, the fetcher stops blaming --to for a version that came from
the manifest, `make upgrade-finalize` passes ARGS through, and the pending and
candidate manifests are gitignored so the "commit your resolved conflicts" step
can't sweep them in.

* fix(upgrade): recover the stamp that makes normalization cancel

`generated_at` is rendered into backend/pyproject.toml and into every alembic
`Create Date:` header. normalize blanks it in all three trees so it cancels out —
but only when it knows the value, and a recovered manifest never carried one.
run_upgrade read None, strip_generated_at returned early, and BASE/THEIRS rendered
the stamp empty while the client's files carried the real one: every stamped file
read as an edit they never made.

Measured on a minimal project — recovered context vs. one generated with a real
stamp — 3 of 208 files differed with zero client edits, one of them
backend/pyproject.toml, which moves on nearly every release. So the guide's
flagship "recover a legacy project" flow opened with a conflict on a file nobody
touched. With the fix: 0.

Alone among the value variables this one leaves a trace, so recovery reads it back
out of backend/pyproject.toml. `None` (no stamp found) and `""` (a project that
genuinely recorded an empty one) are kept apart: the latter is already what the
template renders, so it warrants neither a context entry nor a warning. When it
cannot be found at all the candidate manifest says so, next to the version warning.

Also fixed, all on the same merge-soundness theme:

- format_frontend bailed out whenever the tree already held frontend/node_modules
  — exactly OURS when the client committed theirs, never the freshly rendered
  BASE/THEIRS. That is the uneven-formatting case the FormattersRun warning was
  added for, and the install sitting in the tree is a perfectly good one. Use it in
  place, and leave it alone afterwards rather than unlinking the client's real
  directory. Prettier ignores node_modules without --with-node-modules, so passing
  `.` stays safe. The guide's troubleshooting entry no longer blames a committed
  node_modules for something that now works.
- materialize left directories behind. git tracks files, not directories, so a
  release dropping a whole subtree unlinked its files and left the empty folders
  for good — git checkout prunes them, hand-rolled deletion has to say so. Stops at
  the first parent that still holds anything, so an untracked or ignored file never
  takes its directory down with it.
- _iter_text_files prunes SKIP_DIRS via os.walk instead of filtering rglob's output
  one entry at a time. rglob cannot prune, and restore_generated_at runs over the
  client's *whole* repo, where node_modules alone is routinely six figures of
  entries. The relative-path matching that fixed the ancestor bug is unchanged.

* fix(upgrade): the merge must reach the branch, and the guard must fail closed

Review round on the version-upgrade tooling. Each finding has a regression test
that fails without its fix.

merge:
- An untracked symlink where the template now ships a file was subtracted from
  the staging set as well as from the collision guard. The link was replaced and
  the file written, but `git add` skipped it — the upgrade branch was missing a
  file it claimed to deliver. The two symlink sets are now distinct: tracked ones
  carry the "never deleted, never restaged" guarantee, untracked ones only waive
  the collision guard.
- `tar -x` ran without `-f`, so tar read the archive named by $TAPE instead of
  stdin. With that exported, extraction was a silent no-op (exit 0, nothing
  written) and the old content was staged as if the merge had produced it.
- The collision guard used exists(), which follows the link, so a dangling
  symlink read as absent and was overwritten with no warning — and .gitignore
  keeps such a link out of `ls-files --others`, so nothing else caught it.

rename guard:
- A 404 was read as "no published baseline yet" for either PyPI call, so a 404 on
  the wheel of a version PyPI says exists skipped the guard — the fail-open case
  it exists to block. Only the latest-version lookup can mean "nothing published".
- The suggested block carried get_generator_version(), which mid-cycle *is* the
  baseline, so pasting it turned an "uncovered" failure into a "stale" one. It now
  emits a <next-release> placeholder and says why.

robustness:
- The wheel digest came from a second metadata request; any failure there returned
  None, which the caller reads as "no digest known" — a silent downgrade to an
  unverified download. One request now carries both URL and sha256.
- Prettier's exit code is checked like ruff's, so a tree that fails to format is
  no longer reported as evenly formatted.
- A malformed UPGRADES.yaml block is rejected where the file is read, naming the
  file and the entry, instead of surfacing as a KeyError from one of the three
  consumers that index r["from"] / r["to"].
- read_manifest rejects a non-object `context`.

fix(template): unbreak generated projects against upstream releases (#136)

fastapi-pagination 0.15.16 (2026-07-28) does not work with any FastAPI below
0.140.5, which the template's `fastapi>=0.135.3,<0.137` pin guarantees. It
probes for FastAPI's private _get_body_field / _get_flat_body_params helpers to
pick a call signature, and its ImportError fallback binds the *public*
get_body_field while still setting _get_body_field_new_signature = True. So
add_pagination(app) calls it with a body_params kwarg it does not accept and
app.main raises TypeError on import: every generated project with pagination
stopped starting, and every template CI job went red. Pinned <0.15.16 until
upstream fixes the fallback or the FastAPI pin moves past 0.140.5.

deepagents 0.7 dropped the runtime argument from StateBackend.__init__ and
changed create_deep_agent to take a backend instance rather than a factory, so

first agent invocation would have raised TypeError. _create_backend now returns

has moved between minors, and an unbounded pin turns an upstream release into a
broken generation.

RedisClient.get declared `str | None` and leaned on a type: ignore that no

fix(template): make Docker deployments work off localhost (#132) (#135)

The frontend service in docker-compose.prod.yml passed no build args at all,
and NEXT_PUBLIC_* is inlined into the browser bundle by `next build`, so every
image baked the Dockerfile's localhost defaults. The visitor's browser then
dialled ws://localhost:8000 on its own machine — connection refused, chat input
permanently disabled, status stuck on "Offline" — and no runtime environment
entry could change it. Both compose files now pass the full NEXT_PUBLIC_* set
as build args, defaulting to https://api.${DOMAIN} behind a proxy and to
${PUBLIC_HOST} with the published ports without one, each overridable per
variable.

BACKEND_WS_URL was documented in five places and read in none, a leftover from
when the chat stream went through a Next proxy: the one variable a deployment
could set for the socket was the one variable with no effect. Removed, along
with NEXT_PUBLIC_AUTH_ENABLED, unread since auth stopped being optional.

The auth cookies were Secure whenever NODE_ENV=production, and a browser
silently discards a Secure cookie that arrives over http://. On a plain-HTTP
host login therefore appeared to succeed — the user and token come back in the
body — while every request after it returned 401, /api/auth/me included, so the
access token never refreshed and the socket never reconnected with a good one.
COOKIE_SECURE now makes the flag explicit, and an unrecognized value falls back
to the NODE_ENV default so a typo cannot downgrade production. The six copies of
the cookie block are now one lib/auth-cookies.ts helper with unit tests.

nginx set the Upgrade headers on /ws while the endpoints live under /api/v1/ws,
so the handshake failed on that path too. Same wrong path fixed in the docs.

The white-label brand vars had the same missing-build-arg gap: read by the
browser, never declared as Dockerfile args.

Closes #132

fix(security): close delegated-auth escalation, enforce rate limits, make reset links single-use (#138)

Findings from a full audit of the template's product code. One pattern
underlies most of them: the mechanism is built and correct, and nothing
attaches it. All the worst cases lived in configurations no CI job rendered —
53 of 88 CLI flags were never generated — so nothing was in a position to
notice.

Security:

- Delegated auth kept the local credential endpoints mounted. On a fresh
  delegated deployment the users table is empty until an IdP user first
  authenticates, register() promotes the first row to app-admin, and SQLAdmin
  authenticates on a local password without consulting the IdP — so an
  unauthenticated caller could register and then log into /admin with full
  CRUD. Delegated mode now generates only /auth/me; AdminAuth additionally
  requires is_app_admin and an IdP-linked row.
- get_current_user_ws validated against the local SECRET_KEY in delegated
  mode: IdP tokens were rejected (chat never connected) and locally minted
  tokens were accepted (agent reachable by the account above).
- Rate limiting shipped twice and guarded no route. slowapi had no middleware
  and no decorated routes; make_rate_limit_dep had no call sites and could not
  serve /auth/* anyway because it required CurrentUser. Wired the Redis
  sliding-window service to the auth endpoints, added an anonymous per-IP
  variant, deleted the slowapi copy.
- services/rate_limit could not be imported without --teams (ActiveOrg) or
  without --caching (app.core.cache.get_redis, which never existed).
- Reset and magic links were replayable for their full TTL despite documented
  single use. Reset tokens now bind to the password hash they were issued
  against; magic links carry an epoch that redemption increments.
- Connector secrets used CHANNEL_ENCRYPTION_KEY, which is only declared when a
  messaging channel is enabled — AttributeError on any RAG-only project.

Fixed:

- The warmed cross-encoder reranker was discarded and rebuilt per request, so
  each search reloaded the model. Read it from lifespan state, and declare the
  key on LifespanState.
- WebhookRead.updated_at was non-optional; a never-modified row returned 500.
- get_or_create_from_idp sat inside the OAuth gate, so delegated auth without
  --oauth raised on every authenticated request.
- Four of five AgentSession variants treated unknown control frames as
  prompts, answering "Empty message" to frames the shared frontend always
  sends.

Added CI jobs for delegated auth (both modes), rate limiting (with and without
teams) and RAG + reranker. Replaced `assert limiter is not None` with tests
that assert a 429 actually comes back, plus replay regressions for both link
types.

Also: dropped 8 unused runtime deps from the generator (~20 MB on install),
removed three written-but-unwired modules, stopped two routes calling
repositories directly, and corrected four docs claims describing code that
does not exist.
